audit: I found no credible novel gene-diagnosis associations; every claim I report is an established driver, and I report it as such rather than headlining it as new. Four of the strongest apparent associations are data artifacts and are deliberately excluded: NOTCH2 in Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (19/75), MED12 in Ependymoma, NOS (15/81), NF2 in Pilocytic astrocytoma (13/168) and BCOR in Medulloblastoma, NOS (25/212). In these gene-diagnosis pairs a large share of missense calls are amino-acid substitutions that cannot arise from a single-nucleotide change (e.g. MED12 p.A1285Y, p.E588C; NF2 p.G9396C), versus ~0.06% cohort-wide, and many protein positions far exceed the protein's length (NOTCH2 p.E127469G, NF2 p.P21404E, BCOR p.P130459F), which is impossible for real calls. They look injected or mis-annotated and would not replicate; BCOR is genuinely mutated in some SHH medulloblastomas, but this cohort's BCOR signal is essentially all impossible records. Other concerns: ~10 hypermutated tumors (up to 15,731 mutations, mostly 'Glioma, malignant') can create spurious enrichment for long genes, so I excluded cases with >500 (and checked >200) mutations; many diagnoses are vague or missing ('Neoplasm, malignant', 'missing', 'Unknown', 'Glioma, malignant' mixing DMG/HGG), and overlapping labels (Rhabdomyosarcoma NOS vs ERMS; Craniopharyngioma vs adamantinomatous) dilute signals; most diagnoses have <15 cases so long-tail hits (e.g. CYP4F8, ANO9, FCGBP) are consistent with chance after ~1000+ tests; exome SNV/indel calls miss fusions, CNAs and deletions (KIAA1549-BRAF in PA, SMARCB1 deletions in AT/RT, MYCN/ALK amplification), so expected frequencies understate true alteration rates; one recurrent C17orf80 p.S281R call in 5 unrelated tumor types looks like a recurrent artifact. I would not present any finding from this cohort as novel without independent validation.
methods: Per case binary mutation status per gene (any non-synonymous variant). For each diagnosis label and gene, one-sided Fisher exact test of mutation frequency in that diagnosis vs all other cases, excluding hypermutated cases (>500 mutations; sensitivity check at >200), with rough Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Top hits were checked for record plausibility: missense changes were tested for single-nucleotide reachability using the codon table, and protein positions compared with each gene's typical range; pairs dominated by impossible records were discarded. Remaining significant, biologically coherent hits were reported; probabilities reflect p-value strength, sample size and prior knowledge; expected frequency is the observed rate, lightly shrunk.
